questions.stem: How can bacteria spread antibiotic resistance to other bacteria?

options.text: By absorbing antibiotics and becoming immune
By transferring plasmids carrying resistance genes between cells
By sharing mitochondria during cell division
By developing a thicker cell membrane over time

questions.explanation: Bacteria can transfer plasmids between cells through horizontal gene transfer. If a plasmid carries antibiotic resistance genes, the receiving bacterium also becomes resistant, which is why antibiotic resistance can spread rapidly.
